s003.p: Wrote the first plan: 9 pieces of work plus a final assembly step, 30 requirements (25 of them must-haves), and 122 tests to write.

s006.p: The reviewer found 2 serious problems in the plan and 6 smaller ones. It scored the plan 5 out of 10 on its checklist. The serious problems: the privacy scan could not pass on text that was already public, and some pieces listed the wrong pieces they depend on.

s007.p: Fixed all 8 problems the reviewer raised. It also dropped one risky idea entirely and added two new checks. The plan now has 27 must-have requirements and 146 tests.

s008.p: Six of the earlier problems are fixed and two only partly. The reviewer found 2 new serious problems: an earlier build had no start and stop times recorded, and the quick test run could not finish in under a minute because of fixed waits. It also listed 4 smaller ones.

s009.p: Closed all 8 remaining problems. The plan now has 27 must-have requirements and 100 tests, and a release step was added.

s012.p: No serious problems are left. Two earlier points were still partly open, and the reviewer listed 6 smaller ones about how data is stored and how existing files get changed.

s014.p: The plan is final. All review points are closed, with 27 must-have requirements and 101 tests. A separate independent review of the public copy was added as its own step.

s013.p: Built the safety net: 8 quick tests that pass on the original, untouched code in about 3 seconds. Every later change is measured against them. It also left notes about weak spots for later pieces.

s02A.p: Stopped early because GPT hit its daily usage limit around 9:07 am. The two writers had covered 68 of the 101 tests between them. The same limit stopped this work yesterday too.

s02B.p: Stopped early for the same reason: GPT hit its daily usage limit around 9:07 am, with 68 of the 101 tests covered across both writers.

s030.p: Stopped on purpose. This backup writer (Claude) ran into its own weekly usage limit around 9:15 am and could not go on. The coordinator closed it at 3:10 pm after another writer finished the job.
s030.th: A GPT writer finished the tests.

s045.p: Finished the tests. All 82 tests that run as code are written, plus 9 browser checks written as scripts. A few tests can only be judged by looking at evidence, so those were left for people to check.

s040.p: Stopped on purpose. The builder died when Claude's weekly usage limit ran out around 9:15 am, and it had written nothing. A fresh builder started the piece again.

s044.p: 23 of 24 tests passed. The one failure was a mistake in the test itself (it compared 6:02 pm with 10:02 am), which the coordinator confirmed. The whole test run takes 21 seconds.

s055.p: The checker asked for 6 fixes, though all 24 tests passed. Examples: a folder path written into the code, no warning when a message might contain a secret, and a crash when input is closed.

s058.p: Made all 6 fixes plus three small suggestions.

s060.p: The 6 fixes held and nothing else broke. The checker asked for one more thing: the help text for the log command must list its options.

s065.p: Added the options to the help text, and a missing detail for one kind of logged event.

s068.p: The checker sent it back with 3 more fixes. It did not write down the details.

s072.p: Made the 3 fixes. One test still needed a warning when a step is logged with no open phase.

s075.p: Added that warning. The remaining test passes now.

s046.p: Wrote the instructions and templates. The matching test passes and the safety net stays green. It took 3 minutes.

s047.p: The checker asked for 6 fixes: missing options for naming a run, a path that failed when built from the plan, one wrong sentence in the spec, two lists of vendors that did not match, a README claim that was not true, and an undefined home folder.

s048.p: Made all 6 fixes plus the suggestions.

s049.p: The 6 earlier fixes held. The checker found 3 new things: one way of passing the build name, an example that left the board half empty, and a clash between the optional local model and the roles.

s052.p: A short re-check of only the 3 changes. No further fixes were asked.

s057.p: 11 of 13 tests passed. The 2 that failed need the page piece, which did not exist yet. They pass when a stand-in is used.

s061.p: All 13 tests pass, but the checker asked for 6 fixes in the privacy scan: some changed lines were not scanned, files staged for sharing were skipped, the export scanned files it never copied, the compile check used the wrong Python, a pattern file crashed the scan, and a few allow-list lines were wrong.

s067.p: Worked through the checker's 6 fixes. The builder did not leave a note.

s077.p: 5 of the 6 fixes held. New: a file name starting with a colon slipped past the privacy scan, and one deploy test sometimes fails when the computer is busy.

s080.p: Worked through the new findings. The builder did not leave a note.

s112.p: Made another round of changes. The builder did not leave a note.

s096.p: Wrote the public-copy checklist (55 lines), a row in the README and an entry in the changelog. Packaging the copy for sharing is still to do.

s06N3.p: Stopped on purpose. The coordinator stopped this builder because its test of the notification feature popped up real alerts on Nayan's Mac. The code it had written was kept.

s064N3.p: All 6 start-of-build tests pass. The builder also found an older test that still used the real check by mistake.

s070.p: All 6 tests pass, but the checker asked for 4 fixes: one setting missing from the machine-readable output, settings warnings that were never shown, an unfriendly error for a bad limit setting, and the word 'Ready' shown when nothing had been checked.

s079.p: Made the 4 fixes. The builder did not leave a note.

s081.p: The second review left no note. The next attempt was triggered by a clock problem that the end-to-end test found.

s088.p: Fixed the clock the start-of-build check used. The end-to-end test now correctly stops a build that has gone quiet (0 versus 360 seconds).

s06N4.p: All 8 report tests pass. It left two notes for the pieces built next: how the program reads its command line, and that it works on a private copy of one step.

s063.p: All 8 tests pass and the checker confirmed the numbers by hand against the log. It still asked for 5 fixes, all about how things are shown and rare cases.

s073.p: Made the 5 required fixes plus 3 suggestions.

s074.p: The second review left no note.

s090.p: The end-to-end test passes now, and the 8 report tests still pass.

s06N5.p: All 5 page tests pass. The browser tests could not run because the browser tool was not installed. A manual check for unsafe page content found no problem.

s066.p: Stopped on purpose. The checker's browser tool kept opening visible Chrome windows on Nayan's screen, so the coordinator ended it.

s076.p: All 5 page tests pass. The checker expects two clashes with the browser tests (repeated text and a status shown in the build picker), plus a build name that carries a stray line break. One browser test needs a faster retry or a fix of its own.

s083.p: Made the fixes. The builder did not leave a note.

s084.p: The product code is fine. One browser test has a mistake of its own: it waits 10 seconds while the page also refreshes every 10 seconds, and it reports errors when a request is refused. That is fixed during assembly.

s06N2.p: Stopped on purpose. Its test runs sent real Mac pop-ups to Nayan, because the notification default was not switched off. The code it had written was kept.

s064N2.p: 16 of 18 tests passed. One test was itself wrong (fixed later), and one needs a feature from the step recorder piece.

s078.p: The checker asked for 6 fixes. A secret split across two reads could slip through, an expected-output file was not redacted, a help text was missing, a command could be guessed, some failures were silent, and old-format lines broke the check. It also found why some timing tests failed: stale cached code.

s087.p: Made 6 changes. Some could only be done partly, because the tests require lines without values to still be counted. The quick test run passes in about 32 seconds.

s092.p: 5 of the 6 fixes held. A secret written as key=value could be cut in half when a very long line was split. Also, 2 of 5 quick tests failed because their time limits were very tight (0.3 seconds).

s094.p: Made another round of fixes. The builder did not leave a note.

s095.p: The earlier leak is fixed (3,000+ cases clean), but three other ways a secret could reach disk remain. Output with no spaces was also very slow.

s100.p: A stronger builder (Opus) tried: 5,173 unit cases and 68 end-to-end cases showed no leaks, 18 of 18 tests pass, and a 50 MB output takes 4.4 seconds.

s104.p: The earlier failures are fixed and the output is intact. Two narrower leaks remain: the leftover tail of a dropped token could hide the next secret, and the scanner lost its place between reads.

s106.p: Fixed both leaks within the time limit. The checker's own test set and the builder's own test set were both clean. A 50 MB output takes 4.4 seconds.

s108.p: The checker's test set came back clean, but a randomized stress test still found 3 new rare leaks (4 in 36,000 cases). This is why the owner asked for a simpler redesign of how output is captured.

s111.p: Made another round of changes. The builder did not leave a note.

s085.p: Cleaned up wording in the source so the public-copy privacy scan passes. The tests were only touched mechanically, and only after the coordinator reviewed them.

s091.p: All 9 browser tests failed, but every failure was a mistake in the test scripts, not in the product. Examples: the menu text did not match once an icon was added, the tests did not wait for the first load, and two tests used different clocks.

s098.p: All 9 browser tests pass, twice in a row, without showing a browser window. Screenshots were saved as evidence.

s109.p: Verdict: fix first. It found one serious problem (a runner that keeps files could run in a private folder) and four medium ones: a scan that prints 2 characters, an export that follows shortcuts, a second notification limit being overridden, and incomplete evidence.
s109.th: The fixes were made and tested.

s103.p: Did not finish. The independent reviewer produced nothing for 2 hours because its tool got stuck on sign-in errors, so it was stopped at 5:34 pm. It will be run again on the final copy tomorrow.
s103.th: Rerun planned on the final copy.

plan: Decide what to build and break it into pieces.
plan-review: A second AI company reads the plan and looks for mistakes before building starts.
N0: Quick tests that must keep passing, so we notice if anything breaks.
TW: Write what 'done' looks like before anything is built.
N1: Writes down every step of a build so it can be shown later.
N6: The written instructions people use to run the factory.
N7a: Install the factory on a computer and make sure nothing private gets shared.
N2: Makes the recorder work by itself so nobody has to remember.
N3: Catches setup problems before a build begins.
N4: Turns the record into a short report for each build.
N5: The page you are looking at.
INT: Join the pieces and test the whole thing the way a person would use it.
N7b: Prepare the version that is shared publicly.
PR-REV: A fresh reviewer who has not seen the work reads the public copy.
REL: A last review, then your decision on whether to release.

stages.d: Decide what to build, get a second opinion, and set up a safety net.
Write what 'done' looks like before building anything.
Three pieces that the rest depends on, built side by side.
The main features, built side by side.
Join the pieces together and prepare the public copy.
A fresh reviewer checks the public copy.
A last review, then your decision.

states: This piece cannot start yet because it needs other pieces to finish first.
A builder is making this piece right now.
A different AI is reading the builder's work and looking for problems.
The checker found problems. The builder will fix them in a new attempt.
The checker is satisfied. Nothing more is needed on this piece.
This attempt ended early, on purpose or because something ran out or got stuck. The note says which and what happens next.
Didn't finish (shown as 'failed' in technical details)
This attempt ended with a problem it could not fix by itself, such as hitting a usage limit. The note says why, and another attempt follows.
A decision only you can make. It appears at the top of the page.
How many times a builder has taken a turn at this piece. A piece sent back gets a new attempt.

recent.A decision is needed: GATE B: A decision is needed from you: the release decision.
recent.Public reviewer failed: The independent reviewer did not finish.
